correctness.rationale: For any smooth plane quartic C/F5, a rational line L is a rational bitangent (counting hyperflex degenerations by even divisor) exactly when the binary quartic F|L is a nonzero scalar times the square of a homogeneous binary quadratic over F5. There are 31 rational lines in PG(2,5). The input 31 plane quartic equations were checked entry-by-entry against the original source repository blob 684ea266a0a862882fb8412572efa652889be49b in RationalPoint/excessive's AllGenus3.magma: all 31 expressions match exactly, with no missing/altered entries. Independent SymPy modular polynomial restrictions enumerate all 31 lines on each of all 31 curves, compare normalized coefficient 5-tuples with all 31 projective quadratic-square coefficient signatures, producing 961 fully checked decisions. The exact bitangent numbers in source order are 0,1,1,2,1,2,1,1,2,1,0,2,2,2,2,1,6,1,1,1,1,1,4,2,4,1,1,4,4,0,16. Therefore six distinct realized counts {0,1,2,4,6,16} with frequencies (3,14,8,4,1,1); the unique 16 class is the Fermat x^4+y^4+z^4, with lines (1,b,c) for b,c nonzero. The Faber–Grantham–Howe 31-class input exhaustivity is a named dependency, not newly proved here, and the bitangent scan is exhaustive conditional on it.

originality.rationale: Faber–Grantham–Howe arXiv:2207.14307v2 already give complete isomorphism classes of 31 pointless smooth genus-three curves over F5, and the source input is literally their public code. This assessment never treats the base curve census as a new result. The original paper's relevant §8 curve enumeration and companion original code include equations and zeta data but do not tabulate rational bitangents, and text search found no bitangent theorem. The six-value rational bitangent spectrum and extremal optimizer within that natural exhaustive catalogue is additional contact geometry. Classical Fermat-quartic automorphisms may separately imply its 16 bitangents; novelty of the individual 16 count is lower confidence, but the full six-stratum distribution is not a known-table recomputation in inspected sources.
residual_risks: The 31-class input completeness is inherited from Faber–Grantham–Howe and not independently re-proved.
A historically tabulated rational bitangent spectrum in another source might supersede this novelty; none was found in inspected original fulltext/code.
Bitangent is used in the even-contact-divisor sense including rational hyperflexes; changing the convention could change counts.
